en: A Record of the Miraculous Efficacy and Merit of Reciting the Diamond Sutra:
Formerly, during the Liang dynasty, there was the Venerable Master Yan, a monk at Zhaoti Monastery. When he was first a śrāmaṇera, there was a physiognomist.
He said to Yama, "Though the Lion King was great, intelligent, and wise, what could he do against the King of Signs' short lifespan?
Upon hearing these words,
Yama then invited the Venerable One.
Together let us examine his merit:
what virtuous deeds did he cultivate that he has further gained an extension of his years?
The Venerable One said:
"The sacred words of the Buddha teach that one should receive and uphold the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā* in accordance with the Dharma."
The merit is greatest;
one will surely attain longevity.
At that time, Yan received the command and immediately entered the mountains to receive and uphold the Prajñā Sūtra.
After six years had passed,
he went out again and saw the former physiognomist, who asked,
"Dharma Master, what meritorious deeds have you been cultivating lately?"
That his longevity and extraordinary features could suddenly become such as these—
Yan then explained in detail how he had previously been marked with a short lifespan,
and how he subsequently entered the mountains to uphold the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā*.
There is no other karma remaining.
The Master said,
"It is inconceivable."
By virtue of these merits,
he subsequently became a Great Virtuous One (Bhadanta).
The Dharma Master was over one hundred years of age.
Only then did he receive his final ordination.
During the Liang dynasty, there was Master Sengzang of Kaishan Temple, whose lectures were renowned at the time; there was also Master Yin.
He Yin was highly skilled in physiognomy and divination.
Guojian addressed the Master of the Tripitaka, saying,
"You must be clever in your exegesis.
He then took a scroll at random from within the Sūtra-piṭaka, selecting one intended for the *Dīrghāgama*.
He maintained this practice until he attained the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā*.
He kept it hidden in his room, reciting and upholding it for three years without venturing out.
Later, when he saw Dao-yin, he spoke with joy, saying: "Master, what dharma do you possess that has transformed your appearance?"
The disciple said, "My physiognomy has no sign of efficacy.
Zang said,
"The donor's physiognomy is highly efficacious."
At that time, the fact that he was able to cross over calamities and hardships through the power of upholding the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* was such as this.
Yìn remarked, "This is a fruit of merit and retribution that is truly inconceivable."
Now, more than a hundred years have passed since these signs were obtained;
the harvests have indeed accorded with the predictions as they were spoken.
During the Sui dynasty, there was the Dharma Master Baolun of the Brahman Sangha.
The *Vajracchedikā Sūtra* contains dhāraṇīs and mantras capable of severing all evils.
There was a young monk who studied under me and mastered these incantation methods;
after several years, was he not capable of subduing them?
He went to the riverbank and saw a temple dedicated to a Hu deity;
he sat within its courtyard and recited incantations from memory, whereupon the offender was buried alive.
When Zang heard that his disciple had died, he came in person to the shrine in a fit of resentment.
He also sat in the temple reciting mantras, which resulted in his immediate death.
At that time, there was a monk in the same monastery who constantly upheld the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
Having heard that the Master of the Dharma Treasury and his disciples had both been struck down by a deity, he went to the deity’s abode.
He sat within the temple and recited the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra.
When night fell, he heard the sound of a wind that was exceedingly great and swift.
In a brief moment, he saw an object whose form was extraordinary, magnificent, and most peculiar; it was more terrifying than usual, possessing various shapes and features with eyes like lightning.
The Master sat in right mindfulness, reciting the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* without ceasing, and felt no fear.
The deity came before him and withdrew all his majestic power;
kneeling on his right knee with palms joined in reverence,
he listened until the recitation of the sutra was finished, whereupon the master questioned the deity.
"Who is this deity, the *dānapati*?
At first you arrived with such fierce speed, yet now you remain silent and motionless.
The deity then replied:
"Your disciple is a Hu deity of this palace courtyard.
By nature, he is stubborn and perverse;
yet he has seen that you practice the Mahāyāna sūtras, which are inconceivable."
Therefore, I prostrate myself to listen.
Since you, the donor, are already able to maintain such faith and reverence,
for what reason did the two monks previously reciting mantras strike and kill [the snake]?
The deity said:
"Those two monks were unable to uphold the Mahāyāna sūtras;
when they saw their disciple coming, they met him head-on, reviling him and reciting evil words and incantations."
The disciple did not submit.
When these two monks saw the disciple’s appearance, they were both terrified of death;
it was not because the disciple had intentionally disobeyed that they killed him.
The attendants,
knowing that the Master had entered their shrine to stay overnight,
feared that he would be beaten to death just like the two monks before him.
At dawn, the people gathered together and proceeded to the shrine to welcome him; there they found that he was safe and sound.

When they asked the Master about the circumstances and the details of what had occurred, he answered them fully. Because of this, many among the people were moved to resolve their minds toward awakening and began to uphold the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
In the eleventh year of the Kaihuang era,
Zhao Wenchang, an official of the Taifu Si, passed away; his only aspiration was that he might attain rebirth in the upper realms,
so his family members did not dare to perform the funeral rites immediately.
However, Chang eventually arrived before King Yama,
who questioned him, saying,
"Since birth, what meritorious deeds have you performed?"
Chang said,
"I have no other meritorious virtues;
I do nothing but constantly recite and uphold the Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra."
Upon hearing this, the King joined his palms in reverence and praised him, saying:
"Excellent! The merit of upholding the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā* is supreme and inconceivable."
He then said to the official in charge,
"Examine the records again and do not bring the wrong one.
The man did not hear whether he had indeed brought the wrong one.
He then said to Chang, "Go to the scripture repository and bring the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*; let one person lead the way.
Chang went southwest to the scripture repository.
The great residence I saw consisted of more than several dozen rooms and was exceedingly exquisite and magnificent.
It was filled with scriptures,
all bound in golden covers and fine silk, adorned with such vast splendor and marvelous beauty that words cannot fully describe them.
Chang then single-mindedly closed his eyes and said, "Virtuous One, you are my foremost disciple; once I have experienced this fear, this is no longer Prajñā.
He sought out an attendant to request an exchange, but [the master] would not consent.
Chang opened it and saw that it was indeed the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā*.
He took it to the king's presence and ordered the attendants to stand to the west;
Chang himself stood to the east and recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* once.
He was able to master it thoroughly.
The King then released him with these instructions:
"Chang, you must uphold this sutra and never let it be forgotten."
He was still ordered to be led by one person.
As Chang escorted him out the gate, he saw Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou confined within a room to the east of the gate;
the Emperor called out to him, saying, "You are a man of my own country."
"I have come here for a moment and must speak with you.
Chang immediately saw Emperor Wu and prostrated himself twice.
Emperor Wu said:
"Do you recognize me?
"I do," he replied.
"Your servant formerly held office and served under Your Majesty."
Emperor Wu was delighted and said,
"You are indeed my old friend.
You may return home and speak on my behalf."
Now, as the Emperor discusses the Way, my various offenses are all cleared;
only the matter of the extinction of the Buddha-dharma remains unresolved. At that time, due to the slanderous words of Wei Yuansong, I was unable to remain in confinement for long.
This was not yet understood by Li Chao,
who asked Emperor Wu:
"Wei Yuansong is one who stands outside the three realms."
"He is not under the jurisdiction of King Yama;
for this reason, he could not be caught.
Return home and act as my messenger."
Now, Your Majesty has requested a small portion of merit to rescue us from this suffering and hardship; only then did we dare to hope for recovery.
Chang returned home and regained his life.
Five days have already passed, and his ailment has gradually diminished.
He reported these matters in full to Emperor Wen.
Upon learning of this, the Emperor immediately issued an edict to the masters and monks of all monasteries within the realm,
ordering them to observe a three-day fast and perform ritual services on behalf of Emperor Wu of the Zhou.
He recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* and also recorded it in the *Shiji*.
There was once a man in Suizhou who...
In the first year of the Zhenguan era, he died and was revived after three days.
He recounted that at the time of his death, he was pursued by others, and together with several companions, they arrived before King Yama.
Among them was one monk whom the King saw first and called out to.
"Master, throughout your entire life, what meritorious deeds have you cultivated?
The Master replied:
He was reciting only the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
Upon hearing this, the king immediately rose, joined his palms, and praised him, saying:
"Excellent! Since you have received and upheld the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*..."
"You were destined to ascend to heaven;
for what reason have you mistakenly come here?
Before the King had finished speaking, [the man] replied:
Immediately, he saw celestial garments descend to lead the Master up into the heavens.
The King then covered his seat and asked,
"People of Suizhou, what meritorious rewards have you cultivated since ancient times?"
He said, "Since my birth, I have recited various sutras and diligently studied the writings of Yu Xin and the collected works of the various schools of thought.
Lately, however, I have been studying and reciting the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*."
He still had not yet attained it.
The King asked, "Great sinner, do you recognize him?
He replied:
Although he had read the writings of Yu Xin, he did not actually know him in person.
Wang immediately sent someone to show it to the suffering man,
who then saw a great tortoise with one body and several heads.
People said, "This is Gengxin.
A short time after the tortoise had departed, the King said,
"This man has studied and recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā*."
He then ordered him to be released.
Upon arriving, he saw a man who said, "I am Geng Xin; during my lifetime..."
He delighted in citing various sutras to compose literary works,
or he gave rise to slanders and disparaged the scriptural texts;
now he undergoes the retribution of a great sin, as seen in his current torturous execution like that of a turtle.
Thus he was restored to life.
As he recounted these causes and conditions,
the multitude was moved to grief.
He fully understood this to be true.
Since the land of Suizhou was mostly inhabited by migrants who hunted living beings and took their lives for food, he,
through his contemporary insight and discernment, together with others, mutually resolved to sever the causes of killing and harming.
Upon generating the bodhicitta, they all together received and upheld the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*,
receiving it with faith, making offerings to it, and honoring it.
Wei Zhou’s Qi Yantong had constantly recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā* throughout his entire life.
Previously, while serving as the magistrate of Wulao County under Li Mi,
Yan Tong was sought out for execution after the city was captured by rebels.
He was in a state of urgent fear.
He immediately climbed over the eastern wall of the city and threw himself down into a ravine to seek death.
The ravine was more than a hundred *zhang* deep and precipitous;
yet as he descended from the air, it was as if someone were supporting him, and he did not even realize when he reached the bottom.
He then sat upright and composedly upon a flat rock;
after a long while, he rose, entirely without injury.
Yantong was struck with wonder, feeling a mixture of joy and fear beyond measure, and sighed incessantly.
Since that time, I have personally recognized the great power of the Venerable *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā*.
Having thoroughly understood that the power of this sutra possesses inconceivable and supreme merit,
I have applied my mind with faith and reverence, diligently upholding it and never daring to treat it with contempt.
He constantly obtained karmic rewards and attained immeasurable merit.
The monk Fazang of Baoshi Monastery in Fuzhou was pure and refined in his observance of the precepts.
He was upright by nature.
In the thirteenth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty,
he constructed a monastic dwelling at Luochuan City in Luojiao County.
In more than twenty Buddhist halls, three entrances were aligned; they were constructed with bricks and tiles, adorned with exquisite colors and fine thatch.
There were sixteen-foot unpainted statues, each set comprising eleven distinct items.
There was one life-sized stone statue of Avalokiteśvara and various images for a thousand folding screens.
During the Daye era, he obtained a thousand monasteries;
at that time, he had all the statues moved and installed in the Jia-lan Monastery within the city walls of the prefecture, where their broken parts were repaired and restored to completion.
Furthermore, he commissioned the transcription of all the scriptures, resulting in more than eight hundred fascicles;
he specially prepared long rolls and had them copied at Yue’ai Temple in the capital.
All were mounted on sandalwood rollers and adorned with exquisite beauty.
In the fourth month of the second year of the Wude era, Zang fell ill; after twenty days had passed,
he saw a person in blue robes atop a high pavilion,
holding a scroll of scripture in his hand, who addressed him, saying:
The Dharma Master Zang had made all the meritorious deeds he performed throughout his life excellent and sublime;
however, there remained a slight transgression for misappropriating property belonging to the Triple Gem that had not yet been expiated.
This *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā* in my hand is the foremost and greatest Mahāyāna sūtra.
If you yourself transcribe one fascicle of it,
all your sins shall be completely extinguished.
Upon hearing these instructions, the Tibetan replied at once:
"If my illness is cured,
I shall immediately resolve to produce one hundred copies of the Prajñāpāramitā."
I, your disciple, reflect upon my life thus far: although I have cultivated merit, I have indeed never yet transcribed the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā*.
May all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas now witness my study and realization, and may I never grow lax.
The disciple possesses nothing but these three robes, water jar, and alms bowl.
When he has bared his right shoulder, he offers them all as a final entrustment:
"Venerable Sir, may my disciple’s close acquaintances use this to produce [a copy of] the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā*."

Within thirty-five days, he was able to rise; acting in accordance with his vow, he completed the first copy of the *Bhagavatī-vyākaraṇa* in Śrāvastī and distributed it among various people for circulation, reading, and recitation.

Deeply understanding that the power of this Mahāyāna scripture, the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā, is the greatest, inconceivable, and marvelous, those with the karmic affinity shall successively exhort one another to uphold the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra.
One sees that the merit of obtaining this fruit is immeasurable.
During the Sui dynasty, there was a monk named Lingji who had two disciples.
One day, the Sangha Master suddenly called these disciples forward and said,
"I have heard that on Mount Wutai there is the Great Mañjuśrī."
Whenever anyone comes to pay their respects,
he manifests his physical form to welcome and guide all sentient beings.
We three shall go there to pay our respects.
"Is this not excellent?
I shall load two donkeys with two hundred bolts of raw silk;
I will dispatch my disciples to drive one donkey while I myself mount the other and set forth immediately."
That monk, having been ordained for only one year, maintained nothing but the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* and had no other occupation.
At the time of his departure, he took only this single scroll of the sūtra with him inside a small wooden chest.
After traveling for several months, they rested in a grassy marsh and unyoked their donkeys.
The monk lay down upon a felt mat beneath a tree and fell fast asleep.
His two disciples then discussed among themselves, saying, "We intend to kill our preceptor."
"Each of you take one hundred bolts of silk and a donkey;
entering the capital to enjoy yourselves—would this not be the joy of a lifetime?
Once his mind was set, a disciple took a blade and struck him straight through the waist.
After three cuts had already reached the point where blood flowed, on the fourth cut, [the blade] remained suspended in mid-air;
he could not grasp the knife, nor was it level, nor did it separate from him.
For about the duration of two meals, his Upādhyāya woke up and saw this disciple.
Kneeling with both hands resting upon their swords, they remained silent and offered no reply.
The monk then asked,
"Why did you conceive such evil intentions?"
The disciple knelt with both knees toward him and fully explained his original intention.
"Venerable Master, you may also act as a witness to this transgression.
He then immediately requested a scroll, took out the scripture, and prepared to read it.
There were three knife wounds on his waist,
all cut through until they reached the sutra scrolls;
when people looked at the monk’s waist, [they saw this].
There were three layers of crimson robes, each consisting of several folds;
they were so thick that light could not pass through them, nor were they torn.
Is this not due to the spiritual power of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*?
Formerly, the monk Lingyou of Wengu Monastery in Chang’an died suddenly.
After seven days had passed, he saw King Samatā,
who asked the Master, "What scriptures or practices did you engage in during your lifetime?"
Lingyou replied,
"Recite the Diamond Sūtra.
The king then joined his palms and requested her to recite it.
After a brief moment of reflection, the king asked again.
The Upādhyāya said, "Even though one has recited this sutra, what if there is even one verse missing?
Lingyou replied to the king:
The junior disciple merely recited from memory and did not know which verse was missing.
The King said, "The Master's lifespan has already come to an end;
I grant him ten more years of life."
This sutra is on a stone stele to the west of the city of Haozhou.
Let a true copy be made so that it may be circulated throughout the world.
That monk lived for many years.
He related the circumstances of the matter in detail.
Chen Zhao, a clerk in the administrative office of Hanzhou, died and was restored to life two days later;
he recounted the events as follows:
Upon first arriving in the underworld, the Judge asked:
"For the sake of Official Liu Shangshu, you killed forty-seven oxen;
why did you take one ox from him?"
Zhao avoided mentioning the taboo name.
After a short while, a man came out and said he was delivering ox-heads from Jia; Zhao immediately realized that the taboo name could not be used.
He then consulted the judge on how he might avoid this offense.
The judge asked,
"What meritorious deeds did you perform while alive?
Zhao replied:
He was constantly reciting the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
Before he had finished speaking, the scripture descended from the sky;
he was then allowed to return home and lived for another eighteen years.
If a layperson delights in goodness, they should single-mindedly recite and uphold the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* to give rise to the bodhicitta.
Thus, in a village to the northwest of Xinfan County, he used a brush to write upon empty space to transcribe the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* for heaven.
Whenever it rained in that place, it did not wet the ground;
at first, no one knew why.
A villager was there tending his cattle.
They took shelter from the rain there once more. Later,
a Hu monk passed by, saw them, and said to the villagers:
This is the scripture within the air above the ritual altar;
on the day of the fast, there are often manifestations of precious canopies that appear.
This altar is located thirty *li* northwest of the county seat and remains visible to this day.
In the past, King Dha took countless lives throughout his life;
however, he subsequently resolved his mind to exclusively uphold the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, eventually reciting it five thousand times.
Suddenly, one day at noon, he saw several dozen ghosts approaching him and said,
"The King has issued a warrant for your arrest;
you must cease reciting the sutras for now."
Dharmatā then informed Nianshi, who dispatched a ghost to follow behind. Another ghost messenger arrived on horseback and announced to the ghost:
"The King has issued a decree that the person holding this sutra shall be released. Dharmatā was thus immediately spared from death.
He lived to the age of ninety-eight and then passed away.
Formerly, when Wang Chuo served as the Judicial Official of Tianshui Commandery, Xue Ju rose in rebellion and began executing soldiers;
when it was Wang Chuo’s turn, his sword snapped in pieces.
He further ordered the strongman Song Luo to take a blade and strike him down, but the blade snapped into pieces inch by inch.
Xue Ju marveled, saying,
"What dharma do you possess?"
King Chuo replied, "In my youth,
I recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
This must be due to the power of that sūtra."
Xue Ju then released Wang Chuo.
Terrified, Chuo entered a latrine to hide.
As he recited this sutra, a light appeared within the latrine; seeing the light, the bandits followed it to the latrine.
Seeing him, someone asked, "Who is this?
The latrine attendant replied,
"This is King Chao, who was sentenced to execution by sword but did not die."
The bandits said, "There is no need for you to hide;
all the troops already know.
Hurry back home."
From this, he was able to escape this peril.
In the past, there was Zhu Shiheng,
whose disposition was coarse and evil, and who did not revere the Triple Gem.
He served as the Left Vice President of the State of Liang.
His wife always delighted in goodness and exclusively upheld the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
Whenever her husband was away, she would maintain the recitation of the *Vajracchedikā* with perfect devotion.
Subsequently, when her husband returned from outside and saw this,
he snatched the scripture from his wife's hand and threw it into the fire;
yet when the fire was extinguished, the scripture remained undamaged.
Thereupon, the husband and wife withdrew their sutra scrolls and performed repentance before the Buddha.
Formerly, when Cui Shenchong served as a district magistrate of Xiezhou, he encountered a rebellion during which the regional governor was killed.
Shanchong led more than twenty men, carrying their bows and swords, fleeing toward the city of Kunming; by nightfall, they were unable to find their way.
Shanchong told his soldiers, "Recite the Buddha's name with a sincere heart."
Chong was reciting the Diamond Sutra to himself as he traveled forward on horseback. Suddenly, he saw a torch leading the way ahead.
After traveling several li, the fire extinguished and his ignorance vanished.
He was thus able to reach the city of Kunming;
all of this was due to the power of the scriptures.
Formerly, there was a man named Tang Yan, a common official from Qi County in Zizhou.
He constantly recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāraṇī*.

Once, because he was not careful with his affairs, he was pursued by officials while traveling on the road to Suizhou; as he passed through the territory of his home county, an officer attempted to capture him.
Suddenly, Yan heard a voice from the air saying:
"Tang Yan, you must go quickly!
Yan then looked up and saw a Hu monk;
he immediately hid behind a tree and recited the sutras with a sincere heart.
Dozens of pursuers could not see him face-to-face,
and he was immediately delivered from this peril.
Wei Xu was a man of Qin.
He constantly recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
The unseen spirits pursued him three times but could not catch him;
the King then commanded his messengers to report that he was to be released.
Li Yan was a native of Nanyang Commandery.
He served as a county magistrate’s assistant (xianwei) in Dezhou.
Throughout his life, he maintained the practice of reciting the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
Whenever he recited this sutra, a divine light would appear.
Formerly, when Lady Dou suffered from a headache at night, she ordered her maidservant to fetch a fire from the kitchen; as she spoke, she suddenly saw a torch before the steps.
He then ascended the steps as if it were broad daylight.
The lady’s headache was immediately cured.
There was no one who did not cultivate their minds with utmost sincerity.

All of these are due to the power of constantly upholding the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*. Furthermore, there are many more who have obtained spiritual efficacy through upholding the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*;
however, as the texts would be too numerous, they are not recorded here in full for fear of excessive prolixity.
Based on the preceding evidence,
suppose there were someone who took the seven treasures of the trichiliocosm and used them as an offering;
this would not equal the supreme merit of circulating this sutra.
If there is someone who copies the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, upholds, reads, and recites it,
and also causes others to copy and disseminate it—
this is like one lamp lighting another.
A hundred thousand, ten million lamps will illuminate all dark and obscure places without ever ceasing.
If one can transcribe this text and post it upon the walls of a temple, the merit shall be immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable.
The *Vajracchedikā* in one fascicle outweighs Mount Sumeru; Thus our Emperor uniquely upholds it, thoroughly penetrating all eighty thousand dharma-gates.
With the eye of wisdom and the knowledge of others' minds, he surpasses all in understanding;
While discussing songs today, they are but old melodies— Listen now to the words of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā*.
Emperor Kaiyuan personally annotated this: With a sincere heart, prostrate yourself and do not harbor doubt;
This sutra can eliminate all suffering. Awaken the mind so that the celestial eye may foresee and know;
Do not be led astray by the six thieves of ignorance, Remaining muddled and stubbornly clinging to folly within the day.

Since the Nirvana of the World-Honored One countless kalpas ago, For hundreds of billions of asaṃkhyeya eons, kings and ministers have transmitted the holy teachings. Our Sovereign honors and believes in them, a rarity in this world;
Each month, during the ten days of fasting, he abstains from slaughter, Extensively cultivates wholesome deeds, and ordains monks and nuns.
Born from a womb or an egg, he diligently recollects the Buddha with courageous diligence and great compassion;
weary of seeing the pleasures of the five desires within the palace, he thoroughly understands that the characteristics of the body are empty and precarious.
If even the sovereign of a kingdom can thus awaken, how much more so should ordinary people reflect upon this?
In former times, Tiśya was the sovereign of this land; Seeking the sublime Dharma, he abandoned his consort and practiced asceticism with diligent devotion to the Mahāyāna teachings.
He served as a slave—how could such a person now serve as an official?
The present Emperor is sagely and wise, surpassing all nations; With a single thought or movement of the mind, he perceives everything in advance.
The sacred majesty of the Sage pervades the world; The myriad people find peace, and the four barbarian tribes are settled.
I myself have annotated the profound and subtle meaning of the *Vajra*; All sentient beings, down to the crawling insects, receive and uphold it.
The Dharma-protecting deities are exclusively virtuous and shall respond; The various heavens offer praise, yet they do not act according to their own whims.
A white elephant gallops forth to pay homage at Jingshou Temple; jeweled chariots and canopies surround it in many layers.
Enlightened monks lead the way, holding incense and flowers, while immortals ride cranes, filling the sky as they fly.
Those in the eight difficulties turn back from rebirth to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss; the five turbidities are transformed into a pool of the seven treasures.
The Kaiyuan reign shall endure through kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; The Mowang heretics shall all submit and rely [upon the Dharma].
For ten thousand years and a thousand autumns, may the holy teachings be transmitted;
Just as the celestial robes remain unsullied throughout kalpas, It is simply that sentient beings possess great merit, That they encounter the time when the Buddhas appear as supreme vessels.
The wondrous principle of the Vajra is truly difficult to expound; throughout all the sutras, I have universally proclaimed it.
The Buddha spread golden dust until it filled the earth, intending to purchase Prince Jeta’s garden.
The eight classes of spirits followed the Buddha; the Phoenix Pagoda and Dragon Palaces were filled with transformed devas.
The branches of the Jeta Grove extend to receive the birds’ songs; Beneath them lies the golden-sand spring where he washes his feet.

Those who wish to recite the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* should do so as follows:
First, one must invoke the names of the Eight Great Vajras;
having aroused a heart of utmost sincerity, one should then recite the sutra.
These Eight Vajras will, from this time forth, constantly provide protection for those who uphold the sutra.
First, I respectfully invoke the Vajra Blue Destroyer of Calamities,
the sovereign who can eliminate all the karmic misfortunes and transgressions of sentient beings, causing them to be entirely extinguished, and who presides over the great ocean. Second,
I respectfully invoke the Vajra of Pervasive Poison.
Able to remove the suffering of the feverish poisons of all sentient beings, the Master Who Removes Calamities and Poisons;
third, the invitation to the Yellow Sūtra-Seeking Vajra,
who can cause all that sentient beings seek to be fulfilled according to their wishes, and who bestows the merit of the *kumbha-abhiṣeka*.
Fourth, I respectfully invoke the Vajra of Pure White Water,
the Lord of All Jewels who is able to eliminate all the heat, afflictions, and sufferings of sentient beings so that they are entirely removed.
Fifth, I respectfully invoke the Vajra of Red Sound.
The Lord who can illuminate all sentient beings with light and enable them to see the Buddha, who can generate wind;
the sixth, the Invoked Vajra for Subduing Calamities and Dispelling [Harm],
the Lord who can eliminate the suffering of the three calamities and eight difficulties for all sentient beings, [is represented by] the Vaiḍūrya jewel.
Seventh, I respectfully invoke the Vajra of Purple Wisdom,
the Lord of the Firm Treasury who enables all sentient beings to open their minds, attain awakening,
and resolve upon bodhicitta. Eighth, I respectfully invoke the Great Deity Vajra.
